note: USFS Uwharrie NF (Uwharrie Ranger District), an old homesite by the Uwharrie National Recreation Trail off SR 1146 west of Troy, popular with deer hunters and hiking groups as a base camp. The Forest Service calls it tent camping; directory listings (not the agency) describe undesignated drive-up spots in an open field used by self-contained RVs and trailers. Picnic tables and grills. --Claude
summary: The Forest Service has its own page (recreation/yates-place, 'Site Open'), which the entry doesn't link. Confirmed one vault toilet, no potable water; tables and grills. The page says nothing about a fee, season, reservations or RVs, so the derived free/FCFS/year-round values stand. No Uwharrie alert names it (only cave/mine, alcohol and OHV-trail orders).
flags: Criteria: the Forest Service page describes Yates Place only as 'an attractive destination for tent camping' (also a deer-hunter/hiking base camp) and never mentions RVs or vehicle sites. The inclusion evidence ('drive-up sites where you park RV') rests on TheDyrt/Hipcamp, not the agency. Possibly tent-only.
Website: replace the generic Uwharrie NF page with the campground's own page, https://www.fs.usda.gov/r08/northcarolina/recreation/yates-place.
